name: agent-fs-per-path-permission
body:
Law (prose; assessed by review): the fs tools (`apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp`) SELF-ENFORCE per-path scope. Each tool evaluates the acting agent's EFFECTIVE `edit`-action scope — the ordered combination of the lower-priority configuration, the global rules, and the agent's own opencode 2.x `permissions` entries, with the LAST matching entry winning — and REFUSES any path the entries do not permit. opencode resolves a path matched by no rule to `ask`; the tool instead applies its OWN fail-closed default and REFUSES a no-match path (deny-by-default). The fs scope therefore tracks the agent's `edit` scope: a deny entry the `edit` action honours also refuses the fs operation. The rule set and the candidate path are resolved in ONE consistent frame (the same root), so a grant matches exactly the path it names; and for a code-writer a path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is refused regardless of the caller-supplied directory. The tool-level grant is only the tool's CALLABILITY gate; per-path scoping lives INSIDE the tool, never in opencode's matching of a custom tool's path argument.

Acceptance: a generated code-writer's `permissions` array grants `apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp` deny-by-default — never a blanket `"*": allow` — with its allow entries granted ONLY under `apg/.worktrees/*/` (WORKTREE-ONLY; the repo-root variants are not granted, per `requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only`). The worktree form holds because opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout); the agent-builder template's rule 10 states so. The tool refuses a path outside the acting agent's granted entries AND a path whose last matching `edit` entry is a deny, so an allow with a later sibling deny refuses that sibling path, matching `edit`.

ACCEPTED OPEN ITEM: opencode 2.x documents no acting-agent identity on a tool executor — `execute(input, context)` exposes `progress` and `signal` alone — and a custom plugin tool's permission action is its own tool name, not `edit`, so the central engine does not apply the agent's `edit` glob rules to the tool. How the tool obtains the acting agent's identity and establishes the single frame is therefore verified by unit/int tests against a faked V2 tool context; real-runtime verification is outside this change-set. The enforcement — an out-of-scope, deny-revoked, or main-resolving path is refused, and an unresolvable acting agent refuses every path — is what this law fixes.
